brief: Morgan Stanley Prime Brokerage reports hedge funds posted losses in October, with the average Global long/short fund down 3.1% versus the MSCI AC World's -1.6%, the fourth negative month of 2026. Both long and short alpha eroded (long -3.2%, short -1.3% relative to MSCI), narrowing the YTD long/short spread to +1.8% from +7% a month earlier. Dispersion stayed wide: the 25th-percentile fund is down 4.1% YTD and over 40% of long/short funds are flat to negative for the year. The losses accompanied the largest active long/short de-grossing in global equities in over a decade, funds unwinding about 9% of global gross exposure since late June, led by long selling in AI positions across the US, Taiwan, Japan and Korea. US gross leverage fell to 12-month troughs; midterm-year seasonality points to re-grossing into year-end, but the lack of a 2026 PnL cushion makes that pattern uncertain. Funds rotated out of Momentum into Quality/Size, leaving Russell 2000 short interest above the 90th percentile as a consensus short, and fell underweight AI versus market-cap weight for the first time since the trade began, a risk the report frames as two-sided. Europe's crowded long/short spread posted its worst month in over a decade.
